total:
total Gap #

Upper bounds — holds for every total

  • \(\mathrm{Adv}^{\pm}(f) = \Theta(\mathrm{Q}(f)) \le \mathrm{D}(f) \le \mathrm{bs}(f)^3 \le \mathrm{Adv}(f)^6\)
    Reichardt11 Nisan91 Ambainis02
    Only the two ends are about adversaries: $\mathrm{Adv}^{\pm}=\Theta(\mathrm{Q})$ at one, $\mathrm{bs}\le\mathrm{Adv}^2$ at the other, with the ordinary classical chain in between. So every improvement to Is …? lands here doubled.

Lower bounds / separations — there is a family achieving this

  • \(\mathrm{Adv}^{\pm}(f_n) = \widetilde\Omega\big(\mathrm{Adv}(f_n)^2\big)\)
    witness: \(f_{\mathrm{CS}}\) ABK16 SpalekSzegedy06 Zhang05
    The certificate complexity barrier, $\mathrm{Adv} \le \sqrt{\mathrm{C}^{0}\mathrm{C}^{1}}$, applied to a function built to have cheap certificates and expensive quantum complexity: $\mathrm{Q} = \widetilde\Theta(n)$ against $\mathrm{C} = \widetilde O(\sqrt n)$, so $\mathrm{Adv} = \widetilde O(\sqrt n)$ however the true value falls out. Element distinctness is the older and weaker illustration: a $2$-element $1$-certificate but $\mathrm{C}^{0} = n$, so the barrier gives only $\mathrm{Adv} = O(\sqrt n)$ against $\mathrm{Q} = \Theta(n^{2/3})$.
  • \(\mathrm{Adv}^{\pm}(g^{\circ d}) \ge \mathrm{Adv}(g^{\circ d})^{1.098}\)
    HLS07
    Smaller than the barrier separation, but the only one proved between the two bounds themselves rather than through $\mathrm{Q}$. Take the monotone $g$ on six bits whose minterms and maxterms are the Hamming-weight-three inputs of a function of Kushilevitz's, so $\mathrm{C}^{0}(g) = \mathrm{C}^{1}(g) = 3$; a numerically found negative-weight matrix gives $\mathrm{Adv}^{\pm}(g) \ge 2 + 3\sqrt5/5 \approx 3.341$; both bounds compose, and the barrier caps $\mathrm{Adv}(g^{\circ d})$ at $3^d$.

Written out at How much do negative weights buy the adversary?. The positive adversary is pinned between $\sqrt{\mathrm{fbs}}$ and $\mathrm{fbs}$ on total functions [Ambainis02, KulkarniTal16], so this cell is a proxy for $\mathrm{Q}$ versus $\mathrm{fbs}$.

see also: \(\mathrm{Adv}(f)\), \(\mathrm{Adv}^{\pm}(f)\), \(\mathrm{MAdv}(f)\), \(f_{\mathrm{CS}}\), \(\mathrm{ED}_n\), How much do negative weights buy the adversary? data/relations/03-quantum.yaml
partial:
partial Settled #

Lower bounds / separations — there is a family achieving this

  • \(\mathrm{Adv}(\mathrm{Col}) = O(1) \text{ while } \mathrm{Adv}^{\pm}(\mathrm{Col}) = \Theta(n^{1/3})\)
    witness: \(\mathrm{COL}_n\) SpalekSzegedy06 Zhang05 AaronsonShi04
    The property-testing barrier: if every $0$-input is at relative Hamming distance $\ge\epsilon$ from every $1$-input then $\mathrm{Adv}(f) \le 1/\epsilon$, since both certificate complexities are $O(1)$ under such a promise. \(\mathrm{COL}_n\) has $\epsilon = 1/2$, so the positive adversary is stuck at a constant against $\mathrm{Q} = \Theta(n^{1/3})$; \(\mathrm{SIMON}_n\) is the same story against $\Theta(n)$. This is exactly why the negative-weights version was invented.
see also: \(\mathrm{Adv}(f)\), \(\mathrm{Adv}^{\pm}(f)\), \(\mathrm{MAdv}(f)\), \(\mathrm{COL}_n\), \(\mathrm{SIMON}_n\), How much do negative weights buy the adversary? data/relations/03-quantum.yaml
relation:
relation Settled #

Upper bounds — holds for every relation

  • \(\mathrm{Adv}(f) \le \mathrm{Adv}^{\pm}(f)\)
    Trivial: the positive adversary is the negative adversary restricted to non-negative weights, i.e. a minimisation over a smaller feasible set. Both SDPs are written down the same way whatever the domain and whatever is to be output, so the containment is a fact about relations.
see also: \(\mathrm{Adv}(f)\), \(\mathrm{Adv}^{\pm}(f)\), \(\mathrm{MAdv}(f)\), \(\mathrm{ED}_n\) data/relations/03-quantum.yaml

comp:
\(\mathrm{Q}(f\circ g) = \Theta\big(\mathrm{Q}(f)\,\mathrm{Q}(g)\big)\) partial Settled #

Upper bounds — holds for every partial

  • \(\mathrm{Q}(f\circ g) = O(\mathrm{Q}(f)\,\mathrm{Q}(g))\)
    LMRSS11 Reichardt11
    Via $\mathrm{Q}=\Theta(\mathrm{Adv}^{\pm})$ and the perfect composition of the SDP; no $\log$ factor, in sharp contrast to the randomized case.

Lower bounds / separations — there is a family achieving this

  • \(\mathrm{Q}(f\circ g) = \Omega(\mathrm{Q}(f)\,\mathrm{Q}(g))\)
    HLS07 Reichardt11

Quantum query complexity is the only major measure in this zoo that composes perfectly for partial functions. This is the deep reason the quantum world is better behaved, and the reason $\mathrm{R}^{*}(f)=\Omega(\mathrm{Q}(f))$.

see also: \(\mathrm{Q}_{\varepsilon}(f)\), \(\mathrm{Adv}^{\pm}(f)\), \(\mathrm{R}^{*}(f)\), comp-R data/relations/04-composition.yaml
facts: Perfect composition: $\mathrm{Adv}^{\pm}(f\circ g)=\Theta(\mathrm{Adv}^{\pm}(f)\mathrm{Adv}^{\pm}(g))$, which is how one proves $\mathrm{Q}$ composes.
Being an SDP, $\mathrm{Adv}^{\pm}$ is computable in time exponential in $n$ but polynomial in the domain size.

lo.note:
A single character has sparsity $1$ and $\mathrm{osss} = 1$: the two agree, but neither
grows, so this witnesses no exponent. No function in the zoo has $\mathrm{osss}$ growing
while $\mathrm{spar}$ stays bounded -- indeed $\mathrm{spar}(f) = O(1)$ forces $f$ to be a
constant-size combination of characters, and $\mathrm{osss}$ is then bounded too.
